title: Pacific Life's $58.3 Million IUL Settlement (TEST RENDER)
description: IUL policyholders were promised market-tied growth with a guaranteed floor — but a $58.3M settlement against Pacific Life, finalized May 2026, shows how illustrated projections can diverge from what a policy actually pays out.
sourceCitation: TEST RENDER — sourcing pending (Stage 2 / CourtListener). Documents shown are fabricated test assets, not real evidence.

scenes.captionText: Pacific Life just paid $58.3 million. Here's why.
scenes.narrationText: Pacific Life just paid $58.3 million because of what's written inside your policy illustration.
This settlement was finalized in May 2026, and it's not the only one — multiple carriers are facing similar suits right now.

scenes.captionText: Market-tied growth. A guaranteed floor. That's the pitch.
scenes.narrationText: IUL — indexed universal life insurance — is sold with a promise: your cash value grows tied to the market, with a guaranteed floor so you never lose money. What isn't always explained clearly is how illustrated projections differ from what actually accumulates.
The gap comes from a specific assumption buried in the illustration — the projected crediting rate used to generate the 'example' numbers agents show at the point of sale.

If you hold an IUL policy, pull your original illustration and compare the projected column to your actual statement. If you're a Pacific Life policyholder, the settlement claims process is worth checking.
